scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Finnish tango was introduced to Finland in 1913 by traveling musicians from South America.
The first Finnish tango was composed in 1914 by Emil Kauppi.
Finnish musicians began composing their own tangos in the 1930s.
on_screen: Map: Finland · Europe
Image — MISSING

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Finnish tango is performed at festivals such as the Tangomarkkinat in Seinäjoki, which attracts over 100,000 attendees annually.
The festival includes the coronation of a tango King and Queen.
Themes of Finnish tango lyrics include love, sorrow, nature, and longing for home, often using seasonal metaphors reflecting Finnish folklore.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage — MISSING (use images)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Finnish tango is danced in close contact with emphasis on pelvis, upper thighs, and upper body.
The basic step sequence is SSQQ (slow, slow, quick, quick), with variations like QQS or SQQ to match rhythm changes.
Movements are low and horizontal with optional rises and falls, frequent dips, and rotations.
Watch for Dip, Rotation.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (Xbj5IOB0PK8)
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Danced as couples in close embrace; requires ample space for long steps and fluid movement
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Finnish tango music follows ballroom tango rhythm but incorporates habanera and beguine rhythms during choruses.
The bandoneon was replaced by accordion and drums were added.
Listen for the accordion, drums.
The pulse is not explicitly described; rhythm follows ballroom tango with habanera and beguine influences.

Finnish tango music features accordion-led melodies with drum accompaniment, shifting rhythms between habanera and beguine patterns, and melancholic minor-key vocal lines reflecting Finnish nature and emotional themes.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Notable Finnish tango composers include Olavi Virta, Toivo Kärki, and Unto Mononen.
Olavi Virta is known for 'Punatukkaiselle tytölleni', Toivo Kärki for 'Liljankukka', and Unto Mononen for 'Satumaa'.
Finnish tango is a variation of Argentine tango introduced to Europe in the 1910s.
